fridge: transcribed from knowledge/shelf-life-norms.md (USDA FSIS / FoodKeeper / StillTasty / EatByDate).

key: # A blank column means the norms file gives no window for that storage spot.
# printed=1 means the norm counts from the package's printed date

basis: Ground meats: 1–2 days refrigerated; 3–4 months frozen
Steaks, chops, roasts: 3–5 days refrigerated; 4–12 months frozen
Fresh poultry pieces: 1–2 days refrigerated; 9 months frozen
Fresh fish: 1–3 days refrigerated; 3–8 months frozen
Shrimp / shellfish: 1–2 days refrigerated; 3–6 months frozen
Cooked meat / poultry: 3–4 days refrigerated; 2–6 months frozen
Cooked fish: 3–4 days refrigerated; 4–6 months frozen
Hot dogs (opened): 1 week refrigerated; 1–2 months frozen
Deli meat (opened): 3–5 days refrigerated; 1–2 months frozen
Bacon (opened): 1 week refrigerated; 1 month frozen
Sausage, raw: 1–2 days refrigerated; 1–2 months frozen
Fresh eggs in shell: 3–5 weeks refrigerated
Whole milk: 5–7 days past the printed date; ~3 months frozen
Greek yogurt (unopened): 1–2 weeks refrigerated; 1–2 months frozen
Yogurt (unopened): 2–3 weeks refrigerated; 1–2 months frozen
Hard cheese, opened: 3–6 weeks refrigerated; 6–8 months frozen
Semi-hard cheese (Cheddar, Swiss), opened: 3–6 weeks refrigerated; 6–8 months frozen
Sliced cheese (opened): 2 weeks refrigerated; 6–8 months frozen
Butter: 1–3 months refrigerated; 6–9 months frozen
Leafy greens: 3–7 days refrigerated; 10–12 months frozen (blanched)
Asparagus: 3–5 days refrigerated
Bell peppers: 1–2 weeks refrigerated; 10–12 months frozen
Broccoli / cauliflower: 3–5 days refrigerated
Carrots: 2–3 weeks refrigerated
Celery: 1–2 weeks refrigerated
Corn on the cob: 1–3 days refrigerated
Cucumbers: 1 week refrigerated; freezing not recommended
Green beans: 3–5 days refrigerated
Mushrooms: 4–7 days refrigerated
Onions: 2–3 months whole in a cool, dry cupboard; cut onions 7–10 days refrigerated
Potatoes: 1–2 weeks in a cool, dark cupboard; do not refrigerate raw
Tomatoes: 3–5 days on the counter until ripe, then 2–3 days refrigerated
Zucchini / summer squash: 4–5 days refrigerated
Avocado: 3–5 days on the counter until ripe, then 3–5 days refrigerated
Apples: 4–8 weeks refrigerated; 5–7 days on the counter
Bananas: 2–5 days on the counter until ripe, then 5–7 days refrigerated
Strawberries: 3–5 days refrigerated
Blueberries, raspberries: 5–7 days refrigerated; 10–12 months frozen
Citrus (lemons, limes, oranges): 2–4 weeks refrigerated; about 1 week on the counter
Grapes: 1–2 weeks refrigerated
Pineapple (whole): 3–5 days refrigerated; 2–3 days on the counter
Mangoes: 3–5 days on the counter until ripe, then 5 days refrigerated
White rice (dry): 4–5 years in the cupboard
Brown rice (dry): 6–8 months in the cupboard; 8–12 months refrigerated
Cooked rice: 4–7 days refrigerated; 6–8 months frozen
Dry pasta: 1–2 years past the printed date
Fresh pasta: 4–5 days refrigerated; 6–8 months frozen
Bread (store-bought): 5–7 days in the cupboard; 7–14 days refrigerated; 3–6 months frozen
Flour tortillas: 1 week in the cupboard; 3–4 weeks refrigerated
Ketchup (opened): 6 months refrigerated
Mustard (opened): 12 months refrigerated
Mayonnaise (opened): 2–3 months refrigerated
Soy sauce (opened): 2 years refrigerated
Salsa (jarred, opened): 1 month refrigerated
Olive oil: 1–2 years in a cool, dark cupboard
